text.p: - These are the leading stories in the Angolan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The U.N. Secretary General's special representative to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, met Luanda's diplomatic corps on Thursday to brief them on the progress of the peace process.

Beye told the diplomats the process was entering a crucial phase. He said he hoped UNITA's main representative to the peace process, Isaias Samakuva, would return soon from the interior city of Bailundo with a positive response to recent Security Council demands that UNITA demilitarise and begin handing over its territory to the government.

- A high-level Angolan government delegation has ended a trip to Washington, D.C. The group, including presidential advisor Victor Lima and Vice-Minister of Territorial Administration, Higino Carneiro, met Assistant Secretary of State for Political Affairs, Thomas Pickering on Wednesday. The group was also met by the Director of African Affairs for the National Security Council, Shawn McCormick.
